clue.text: To be entertaining when topless is bewildering!

indicators.note: a topless word has lost its head, so its opening letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone finds it baffling that a show could be fun once its star has gone topless.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemusing means puzzling or confusing someone, a direct synonym of bewildering.

clue.text: Fail to see motorway two seconds after

parts.note: the M1 motorway, written with the letter I standing in for the figure 1
S is the abbreviation for second, taken twice

explanation.surface: A driver on the motorway misses something in a couple of seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; crosswords often write it MI.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something is to overlook it or not notice it at all, an everyday synonym.

clue.text: Design it to go round pole in front of hospital department

indicators.note: in front of means placed ahead, so one piece comes before the next
going round something means encircling it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: An instruction to an architect: plan the building round a pole, ahead of the hospital's department.
explanation.definitionFit: A design in the sense of a purpose or aim is an intent, as in doing something by design.

clue.text: One politician to ring rest about cheat

indicators.note: about suggests turning round and moving things into a different order

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A politician phones around the others about someone cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposter is a fraud who pretends to be someone else, so a person who deceives is a cheat.

clue.text: Accountant lied about brat having graduated

indicators.note: the word lies is placed around the other piece, wrapping about it

explanation.surface: An accountant lied about a spoilt child getting a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graduated' looks like finishing university, but it means marked with a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A graduated measuring vessel is marked with a scale of degrees, which is what calibrated instruments carry.

clue.text: Starts running, if man finds firearms!

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

explanation.surface: A man takes off running when he comes upon some guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Rifles are long-barrelled guns, so they are one kind of firearm.

clue.text: Novice wanted to pray inside

parts.note: to beg is to plead or pray for something wanted

explanation.surface: A newcomer to a religious order wants to pray indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is someone new to an activity, a learner just starting out.

clue.text: Endlessly collecting dried fruit

indicators.note: something endless has had its tail cut off, so the final letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone forever gathering up dried fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this is a grape dehydrated in the sun, one of the commonest kinds.

clue.text: Intend, that is, to find a miser

parts.note: to mean to do something is to intend it

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to track down a skinflint.
explanation.definitionFit: A meanie is a stingy, ungenerous person, informally the same as a miser.

clue.text: Sea bird driving back other sea birds

indicators.note: driving something back sends it the opposite way, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: the skua is a predatory seabird

explanation.surface: One seabird chasing off a flock of others.
explanation.walkthrough: Skuas really do chase other seabirds to steal their food, so the surface is natural history.
explanation.definitionFit: Auks are diving seabirds such as puffins and guillemots, a different family from the skua.

clue.text: Real idiots re-writing newspaper articles

indicators.note: rewriting text produces a new version with things moved about

explanation.surface: A jab at the fools who rewrite the opinion pieces in a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Editorials are the leader columns in which a paper's editors state its opinion.

clue.text: Stake placed outside sick quarters

indicators.note: one word is set around the outside of the other

explanation.surface: A wooden post set up outside the sick bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stake' suggests a wooden post, but it is the gambling sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet is lodging for soldiers, so it means living quarters.

clue.text: Entertaining women alight to go to the toilet

parts.note: to alight is to come down and land
the ladies is the women's toilet

explanation.surface: Women hosting a party get off the train and head for the loo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining' means taking in guests, not being amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Landladies are women who take in lodgers, hosting paying guests in their homes.

clue.text: Hobby to arouse curiosity

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pastime someone pursues
second meaning: the verb, to engage someone's attention

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a hobby that makes people curious; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a pastime and a verb for catching someone's attention.

clue.text: Sex information the German is after

explanation.surface: A German man is chasing information about sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Gender is the category of male or female, a synonym of sex in that sense.

clue.text: Record-making company allowance to one settling abroad

parts.note: a grant is an allowance of money

explanation.surface: A record label gives an allowance to someone moving overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant leaves their homeland to live permanently in another country.

clue.text: Writer Elizabeth leaves man to squirm

indicators.note: when someone leaves they go, so her letters are taken away

explanation.surface: A writer called Elizabeth walks out on a man, leaving him wriggling.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist the body about in pain or discomfort, just as you squirm.

clue.text: Famous mathematician has seen it moving at home

indicators.note: moving things about puts them in a different order

explanation.surface: A great mathematician has watched something move about his house.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein, best known as a physicist, did his celebrated work through mathematics such as relativity.

clue.text: River always seen between two points

indicators.note: something seen between two things is set inside them

parts.note: south and north, compass points; these hold the other piece

explanation.surface: A river that is always flowing between two places.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn is Britain's longest river, running through Wales and western England.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Britain's longest waterway flows from mid-Wales to the Bristol Channel.

clue.text: Capital on notice deposited in central Greece

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
the central part of a word is its middle, so only those letters stay

explanation.surface: A capital city's notice is lodged in the middle of Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: Adelaide is the capital of the Australian state of South Australia, not of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is a state capital in Australia, so this definition works by example.

clue.text: I'd peep round for some port!

indicators.note: turning round moves things into another arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone would sneak a look around for a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieppe is a French ferry port on the Channel coast, so a port by example.

clue.text: Study inside of craft, being intensely enthusiastic

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room

explanation.surface: Someone closely studying the inside of a boat with great zeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate and eager, full of fervour for something.

clue.text: Express agreement since forwarded

parts.note: as can mean since, giving a reason

explanation.surface: Saying yes because something has been passed on.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to say yes or consent formally to a proposal.

clue.text: Sore head? You need sympathy!

explanation.surface: Someone with a headache is told they need some kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the body part but it is a headland, a ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderness is gentle warmth and compassion shown to another, close to sympathy.

clue.text: A snack is a bit of a habit, easily broken

indicators.note: a bit of the following words means only part of their letters are used
the run of words is broken open so a stretch inside can be lifted out

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Snacking is a habit that is easy to break.
explanation.definitionFit: A bite to eat is a small quick meal, which is what a snack is.

clue.text: Bowled short, a disappointment

explanation.surface: A cricketer bowled out for a low score is a let-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowled short' sounds like a short-pitched delivery in cricket, but the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow is a setback or shock, something that comes as a disappointment.

clue.text: Bad temper shown when interviewed about page 50

indicators.note: the first word goes around about the others

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper in an interview about a newspaper page.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleen means ill humour or anger, from the old belief that the organ caused it.

clue.text: Nixon to mix carbon, which is not poisonous

indicators.note: mixing things jumbles them into a new order

explanation.surface: President Nixon is told to mix in some carbon, which is harmless.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-toxic substances are harmless if swallowed, so the word means free of poison.
